## Overview
Note first: all per-90 figures are drawn from 810 minutes across 9 appearances, so treat every rate as indicative rather than settled. Kasper Hartly Kiilerich is a 20-year-old goalkeeper at Viborg FF in the Denmark Superliga. His numbers this season are broadly encouraging for a development-stage player, with stand-out figures in distribution and duels, but the sample is too thin and the league level too far below Premier League standard to justify anything stronger than continued monitoring.

## Key Strengths
- **Distribution accuracy:** Pass accuracy of 80.73%, rank 2 of 10 in the peer group (top 20%), suggesting a composure in possession that is worth noting — though the peer group is only 10 players, so treat the ranking as indicative.
- **Duel Win %:** 100%, rank 1 of 10 (top 10%). The sample caveat applies, but no duels lost across this season's minutes is a clean record at minimum.
- **Goals conceded/90:** 0.89, rank 2 of 10 (top 20%). As noted in the GOALKEEPER NOTE, this reflects the whole defence and shot volume; it is context, not a verdict on Kiilerich personally.

## Areas for Development
- **Long Balls/90:** 10.33, rank 10 of 10 — bottom of the peer group. The numbers suggest heavy reliance on long distribution, which may indicate a limitation in playing short or building from the back, though this requires live scouting to confirm.
- **Saves/90:** 2.78, rank 4 of 10 (top 40%) — mid-table in the peer group. Solid but not exceptional, and without post-shot xG data we cannot assess shot-stopping quality against difficulty faced.
- **Missing data:** No post-shot xG, claiming or sweeping data recorded; a full picture of his shot-stopping and sweeper-keeper qualities is unavailable.

## Style of Play (from the data)
The numbers suggest a keeper who keeps the ball well at short range (80.73% pass accuracy, top 20%) but leans heavily on the long ball (10.33/90, rank 10 of 10). Whether that reflects instruction or personal preference cannot be determined from the data alone.

## Data Confidence & To Verify
- 810 minutes across 9 appearances is a small sample; all per-90 rates are indicative.
- The Denmark Superliga sits well below Premier League standard; the step up is significant and must be weighed accordingly.
- No post-shot xG, sweeping or claiming data available. Live scouting must assess shot-stopping quality, footwork under pressure, and command of the box.

## Comparable Profiles
- **Andreas Hansen (Nordsjælland, 31, €1.0M):** Similar saves/90 (2.89 vs 2.78) and pass accuracy (79.19% vs 80.73%), but 11 years older — a very different proposition in terms of resale and development.
- **Patrick Pentz (Brøndby IF, 29, €2.0M):** Higher pass accuracy (82.87%) and comparable saves/90 (2.75), but concedes more (1.75/90 vs 0.89) and is valued at double the fee.
- **Aske Leth Andresen (Silkeborg IF, 21, €0.6M):** Nearest in age, but pass accuracy of 64.32% is well below Kiilerich's 80.73%; similar age profile at a lower price point.

## Contract & Market Context
Kiilerich is contracted until 31 December 2028, leaving 27 months remaining — Viborg hold reasonable leverage. Market value is estimated at €1.0M, which is modest and potentially accessible, but no fee has been agreed or approached. The next available window is January 2027; there is no basis for earlier action.

## Recommendation
Monitor. The distribution numbers and duel record are worth tracking, but 810 minutes in a league at this level is insufficient to justify a firm approach. Assign a scout to attend at least three further matches before January 2027. If the profile holds across a larger sample, revisit ahead of the January window.
resp.risk_rationale: A 20-year-old goalkeeper with only 810 minutes (9 appearances) this season in a league well below Premier League standard, with no injury history on record but an extremely small sample, makes this a high-risk profile on current evidence alone.

## Overview
Brian White is a centre forward whose numbers this season suggest a penalty-box finisher rather than a link-play striker. Across 1,995 minutes (24 appearances), a usable sample, he posts 0.77 goals/90 (rank 7 of 53 in MLS, top 13%) and 1.89 shots on target/90 (rank 4 of 53, top 8%). The profile is convincing within MLS, but the step up to Premier League level is significant and must temper any enthusiasm.

## Key Strengths
- **Goals/90: 0.77 (rank 7 of 53, top 13%).** Among the more reliable finishers in the division this season; the output is consistent across a meaningful minutes tally.
- **Shots on Target/90: 1.89 (rank 4 of 53, top 8%).** The numbers suggest he tests goalkeepers frequently and with discipline; this is a genuine, data-backed strength.
- **Aerials Won/90: 1.67 (rank 22 of 53, top 42%).** Middling but not a weakness; suggests he can compete in the channel without being a dedicated aerial target man.

## Areas for Development
- **Successful Dribbles/90: 0.14 (rank 49 of 53, top 92%).** A significant red flag. The numbers suggest he contributes almost nothing in terms of carrying or beating a man; this will be exposed against higher defensive lines.
- **Assists/90: 0.09 (rank 38 of 53, top 72%).** Offers very little as a creative outlet; the numbers suggest a striker who relies entirely on others to supply him.
- **Key Passes/90: 1.08 (rank 25 of 53, top 47%).** Mediocre hold-up and combination play inferred from the data; not a striker who fits a progressive passing system.

## Style of Play (from the data)
The numbers suggest White is an area striker: he gets into positions to shoot and converts at a solid rate, but he does not carry the ball, rarely assists, and offers limited creative involvement. He is unlikely to suit a press-heavy system that demands a centre forward to initiate press triggers or link play; to verify with live scouting.

## Data Confidence & To Verify
- The sample size (1,995 minutes) is usable but all minutes are in MLS, a step below Premier League standard; goal and shot numbers will need discounting.
- Pressing output, defensive work rate, and physical metrics are not recorded; live scouting must assess suitability for our system.
- Medical team must review the five injury absences since January 2025, specifically the two muscle injuries (30 days missed from August 2025; 41 days from January 2025) and two concussions (2024), before any approach is sanctioned.

## Comparable Profiles
- **João Klauss De Mello (LA Galaxy, 29, €2.5M):** Outperforms White on goals/90 (0.92 vs 0.77) and shots on target/90 (2.09 vs 1.89); a stronger finisher by the numbers and cheaper.
- **Sam Surridge (Nashville SC, 28, €8.0M):** Lower goals/90 (0.88 is still above White) and lower shots on target/90 (1.65); priced at €8.0M but three years younger — better age profile for a Premier League transfer.
- **Tom Barlow (Cincinnati, 31, €0.3M):** Lower across all attacking metrics; confirms White is the stronger performer of the three in pure output terms.

## Contract & Market Context
White's contract runs to December 2027, leaving 15 months on the deal. Vancouver hold leverage but will be aware the market value sits at €5.0M, which is modest. No window is currently open; January 2027 is the next realistic approach point. A loan with an option would reduce risk given the injury history and the question marks around his ability to cope with the step up.

## Recommendation
Approach in January. White's finishing numbers within MLS are legitimate, but the injury record — five absences in under two years, including two muscle injuries — demands a medical sign-off before any commitment. The dribbling and creativity numbers are poor and may limit his usefulness in our system. A short-term loan in January 2027, with a conditional purchase clause, is the most sensible structure if live scouting confirms the basics. Do not pay a straight fee at this stage.

## Overview
Caution required on sample size: all per-90 figures below are drawn from just 630 minutes (7 appearances) and must be treated as indicative only. Jan Plug is a 21-year-old left-footed centre-back currently on loan at Excelsior from Feyenoord, operating in the Eredivisie. The numbers suggest a progressive ball-player who contributes to defensive actions at a reasonable level but carries a significant concern around duels.

## Key Strengths
- **Long passing volume:** 8.14 long balls/90, rank 5 of 35 (top 14%) — the standout figure in his profile; the numbers suggest he is comfortable driving play out from the back.
- **Interceptions:** 1.86/90, rank 9 of 35 (top 26%) — reads play at an above-average level for the league.
- **Pass accuracy:** 90.25%, rank 12 of 35 (top 34%) — combined with the long-ball volume, this points to a centre-back who moves the ball cleanly rather than just clearing his lines.

## Areas for Development
- **Duel win rate:** 47.06%, rank 31 of 35 (top 89%) — bottom quartile in the league; at Premier League pace and physicality this is a serious concern that cannot be dismissed.
- **Aerial threat:** 1.29 aerials won/90, rank 25 of 35 (top 71%) — below the Eredivisie midpoint for centre-backs; a step up in quality of strikers will test this further.
- **Clearances:** 4.86/90, rank 13 of 35 (top 37%) — mid-table; not a weakness but offers no comfort when placed alongside the duel and aerial numbers.

## Style of Play (from the data)
The numbers suggest Plug is deployed as a ball-playing centre-back who is asked to initiate from deep. His long-ball rate (rank 5 of 35) and pass accuracy (90.25%) are consistent with a centre-back comfortable in a back four that builds out. His interception numbers suggest reasonable positional awareness, but the duel win rate raises questions about his ability to compete physically in one-v-one situations.

## Data Confidence & To Verify
- 630 minutes is insufficient for reliable per-90 rates; a minimum of 1,500 minutes is preferred before acting on these numbers.
- The Eredivisie represents a step below Premier League standard; how these metrics translate under greater intensity and physicality is unknown.
- To verify with live scouting: defensive positioning, recovery pace, aerial contest technique, and composure under press.
- Medical team must conduct full physical assessment; no injury history is on record but none has been verified independently.

## Comparable Profiles
- **Wouter Goes (AZ Alkmaar, €15.0M):** matches Plug's interceptions (1.86/90) but is considerably stronger in the air (1.71 aerials won/90 vs 1.29) and commands a valuation ten times higher — the ceiling reference.
- **Julius Dirksen (Go Ahead Eagles, €1.5M):** higher interceptions (2.45/90) and clearances (5.27/90) at the same valuation; defensively more productive on current numbers.
- **Maas Willemsen (SC Heerenveen, €4.5M):** lower across all three comparable metrics (1.0 interceptions, 0.71 aerials, 3.14 clearances); Plug compares favourably here but Willemsen carries a higher price tag.

## Contract & Market Context
Plug is on loan at Excelsior; parent club is Feyenoord. His contract expires 30 June 2027, leaving nine months on his deal, which means any approach must go through Feyenoord — not Excelsior — and will require establishing whether Feyenoord intend to sell or recall. Market value is estimated at €1.5M. No transfer window is currently open; the next opportunity to move is January 2027.

## Recommendation
Do not move yet. The sample is too small, the duel win rate (47.06%, rank 31 of 35) is unresolved, and the loan structure adds a layer of complexity around Feyenoord's intentions. Place Plug on the monitored list, commission two live scouting visits before the end of the calendar year, and review the full picture ahead of January 2027 to decide whether an approach to Feyenoord is warranted.
